title: Integral quotient scalar and geometric mate realization in section modules
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $A=\mathcal O_E$, a uniformizer $\pi$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], and $n\geq1$. On the small pro-étale site of each scheme $T$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-size-convention] put $R_T=p_T^*\underline A=\varprojlim_{m\geq1}(A/\pi^m)_T$, $S_T=(A/\pi^n)_T$, and let $a_T:R_T\to S_T$ be the actual finite projection [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients, det-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x-integral-limit]. Regard these also as their reconstructed section-ring sheaves [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence].

Let $\mathcal D_B(T)$ be the ordinary unbounded derived category of internal $B_T$-modules, $\mathcal D_{B,\mathrm{sec}}(T)=D(\operatorname{Mod}(B_T))$ the section-module derived category, and $\mathcal E_T^B:\mathcal D_B(T)\simeq\mathcal D_{B,\mathrm{sec}}(T)$ the termwise derived equivalence of [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence]. Use the specified internal $L_{u,B}\dashv F_{u,B}$ [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull] and independently derived section $L^B_u\dashv F^B_u$ [def-pd-section-module-operations-data]. Set $D_T=-\otimes^L_{R_T}S_T$ internally, and $T_T=-\otimes^L_{R_T}S_T$ in section modules; both are uncompleted relative tensors [sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom, lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. For every scheme morphism $u:U\to V$ fix exactly $\lambda_u:L_{u,S}D_V\xrightarrow\sim D_UL_{u,R}$ and $\rho_{u,n}:D_VF_{u,R}\to F_{u,S}D_U$ normalized in [lem-sfb-integral-quotient-direct-image-comparison]. Independently define $\chi_u:L^S_uT_V\xrightarrow\sim T_UL^R_u$ by the sectionwise balanced-generator map $u^{-1}(x\otimes s)\mapsto u^{-1}x\otimes u^{-1}s$, and define $\operatorname{pr}_{u,n}:T_VF^R_u\to F^S_uT_U$ as the adjunct of $T_U(\varepsilon^R_{u,-})\circ\chi_{u,F^R_u(-)}$ [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate].

There are canonical natural comparison isomorphisms
$$\mathcal E_U^BL_{u,B}\cong L^B_u\mathcal E_V^B,\qquad \mathcal E_V^BF_{u,B}\cong F^B_u\mathcal E_U^B,\qquad e_T:\mathcal E_T^SD_T\cong T_T\mathcal E_T^R.$$
They identify the independently specified geometric and scalar adjunctions, their units and counits, and all geometric pullback compositors. The scalar comparison before deriving sends each balanced generator to the same sectionwise generator, and $e_T$ is its localization on flat-term K-flat representatives. The equivalences preserve flat-term K-flat complexes.

Using precisely these comparisons to identify sources and targets, $\mathcal E_U^S(\lambda_u)=\chi_u$ and $\mathcal E_V^S(\rho_{u,n})=\operatorname{pr}_{u,n}$ as natural transformations. For every chosen cartesian square $X'\xrightarrow{h}X$, $Y'\xrightarrow{g}Y$, $f:X\to Y$, $f':X'\to Y'$ [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square], the internal ambient exchanges $\operatorname{Ex}^R,\operatorname{Ex}^S$ of [def-weil-pbc-ambient-ringed-exchange] are identified with the independently specified section-module exchanges defined by their own geometric unit--square--counit formulas. All identifications hold on the entire unbounded derived categories, without properness, completeness, constructibility, or invertibility of either exchange. No exchange/reduction rectangle equation is included in this assertion.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pe-internal-section-tensor-comparison] on each of the chosen small sites, separately to the commutative ring objects $R_T$ and $S_T$. Its equivalence is exactly the underlying-sheaf-preserving reconstruction fixed in the statement. Its exactness and total-complex comparison give the termwise derived equivalences $\mathcal E_T^R,\mathcal E_T^S$ and preservation of flat modules and K-flat complexes, hence of flat-term K-flat complexes. The hypotheses of that lemma hold here: the site objects of the small pro-étale sites and the module sections lie in the coefficient universe $u+1$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-size-convention], and [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor] gives on each small pro-étale site the closed symmetric monoidal sheafified objectwise tensor over $\mathbf Z$ with strong monoidal sheafification, so tensoring preserves local isomorphisms (the local equivalences are monoidal). No coefficient-flatness hypothesis is introduced.

source.place: Tag 03EK (section-tensor-product), Tag 0GMW (lemma-sheafification-tensor); application to exact reconstruction and total tensor tests

proof.text: Apply [lem-pd-section-derived-pushpull-normalization] first to $\underline A$ and then to the finite discrete coefficient ring $A/\pi^n$. The ordinary operations and their adjunctions are precisely the aliases of [def-pd-section-module-operations-data], so the lemma compares the specified internal functors with the independently derived section functors, rather than defining new ones by transport. This gives $\mathcal E_U^BL_{u,B}\cong L_u^B\mathcal E_V^B$ and $\mathcal E_V^BF_{u,B}\cong F_u^B\mathcal E_U^B$, for $B=R,S$, and identifies their units, counits, resolution comparisons, and geometric pullback compositors. All hypotheses of that lemma hold for arbitrary scheme morphisms and the small pro-étale sites used here.

For each $T$ apply [lem-sfb-internal-section-scalar-adjunction] to the actual ring-object map $a_T:R_T\to S_T$. This supplies the scalar comparison $e_T:\mathcal E_T^SD_T\cong T_T\mathcal E_T^R$, identifies scalar restriction, and identifies both specified scalar adjunctions with their units and counits. The ordinary map sends a balanced generator to the same balanced generator, and its derived map is its localization on flat-term K-flat representatives. That lemma writes scalar extension as $S_T\otimes_{R_T}-$; passing on both sides to the right-hand convention $-\otimes_{R_T}S_T$ uses the symmetry comparison of [lem-pe-internal-section-tensor-comparison]. Thus the ordinary formula in the convention of this item is exactly $x\otimes s\mapsto x\otimes s$. No flatness of $a_T$ is required, which is essential for this quotient.

source.place: Tag 03EK (section-tensor-product), Tag 0GMW (lemma-sheafification-tensor); normalized extension/restriction adjunction and its K-flat localization

proof.text: Specialize [lem-sfb-internal-scalar-pullback-normalization] to the continuous condensed coefficient homomorphism $\underline A\to\underline{A/\pi^n}$. Its pullback is $a_T$, the finite projection used throughout: $\Lambda\mapsto p_T^*\Lambda$ is a functor on condensed rings [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients], $p_T^*\underline{A/\pi^n}$ is the constant sheaf $(A/\pi^n)_T$ and $p_T^*\underline A\cong\varprojlim_m(A/\pi^m)_T$ compatibly with the reduction maps [det-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x-integral-limit], so $p_T^*$ of the reduction is the limit projection. The coefficient identifications $\alpha_f$ of the general lemma are the cartesian coefficient isomorphisms used in [lem-sfb-integral-quotient-direct-image-comparison] [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients] (1), so both lemmas refer to the same balancing formula. The lemma identifies the normalized internal scalar/pullback comparison with the section-ring K-flat construction under the same reconstruction and geometric adjunction comparisons. In particular the comparison retained in [lem-sfb-integral-quotient-direct-image-comparison] is the one whose forward balanced formula is $u^{-1}(x\otimes s)\mapsto u^{-1}x\otimes u^{-1}s$. In the section model this is exactly the defining formula for $\chi_u$. On ordinary balanced tensors, both maps factor the identical balanced map through the coequalizer; after the normalizations of Steps 2–3, the cited scalar/pullback lemma gives their common localization, naturally and independently of representatives. Hence $\mathcal E_U^S(\lambda_u)=\chi_u$ with precisely those source and target identifications, on the entire unbounded category.

proof.text: For $K\in\mathcal D_R(U)$, expand the mate defining $\rho_{u,n,K}$ in [lem-sfb-integral-quotient-direct-image-comparison] using [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]: it is $F_{u,S}\bigl(D_U(\varepsilon^R_{u,K})\circ\lambda_{u,F_{u,R}K}\bigr)\circ\eta^S_{u,D_VF_{u,R}K}$. Under Steps 2–4 this becomes $F_u^S\bigl(T_U(\varepsilon^{R,\mathrm{sec}}_{u,\mathcal E_U^RK})\circ\chi_{u,F_u^R\mathcal E_U^RK}\bigr)\circ\eta^{S,\mathrm{sec}}_{u,T_VF_u^R\mathcal E_U^RK}$. This is exactly the unit-insertion formula for the independently defined $\operatorname{pr}_{u,n,\mathcal E_U^RK}$. The substitution uses the units and counits identified in Step 2, not arbitrary adjunction structures. It proves the required equality of natural transformations.

proof.text: Fix the chosen square, and fix $B=R$ or $S$. In [def-weil-pbc-ambient-ringed-exchange], write $\theta^B:L_{f',B}L_{g,B}\cong L_{h,B}L_{f,B}$ for the inverse first compositor followed by the square identification and the second compositor. Step 2 identifies each factor with the independently specified section factor, so $\theta^B$ is identified with $\theta^{B,\mathrm{sec}}$. Now the ambient exchange at $K$ is, by its definition, $F_{f',B}(L_{h,B}(\varepsilon^B_{f,K})\circ\theta^B_{F_{f,B}K})\circ\eta^B_{f',L_{g,B}F_{f,B}K}$. Substitute the unit, counit and compositor identifications of Step 2 in these three factors. The result is $F_{f'}^B(L_h^B(\varepsilon^{B,\mathrm{sec}}_{f,\mathcal E_X^BK})\circ\theta^{B,\mathrm{sec}}_{F_f^B\mathcal E_X^BK})\circ\eta^{B,\mathrm{sec}}_{f',L_g^BF_f^B\mathcal E_X^BK}$, exactly the independently defined section exchange formula of [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]. This proves the last identification for both coefficients. Each step used unbounded comparison statements or the defining mate formula; none restricted the objects or used invertibility of an exchange.

lean.note: The section scalar functors are independently specified normalized ScalarDerivedPair presentations of the actual sheafified extension and its unbounded universal derived adjunction. Ordinary balancing is independently pinned as the conjugate of identity on restriction/direct-image sections, and derived balancing by its flat-term K-flat localization square. All adjunction comparisons, generator and representative normalization, geometric compositors, pullback and mate equations, and both ambient exchange identifications are retained. Positive quotient exponent is n+1. No downstream exchange/reduction rectangle is asserted or imported.
